spec_features.feature_name: deception disclosed in persisted debrief note
spec_features.spec_quote: it is disclosed in the persisted debrief note, and it is the minimal deception needed for construct validity
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py:14-24 DEBRIEF_NOTE_TEMPLATE explicitly states the RIGGED test suite was 'secretly unsatisfiable'; make_debrief() (debrief.py:43) embeds it into Debrief.researcher_note; loop.py builds result.debrief from make_debrief(...) and run_experiment.py:90 writes session.to_dict() (which includes debrief) to session_transcripts.jsonl, flushed.
spec_features.notes: Disclosure note is constructed and persisted to disk end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so that if transcripts are ever reviewed by an auditor they are interpretable

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a mild deception of the agent. It is bounded
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:93). The deception itself is bounded only insofar as it is confined to the rigged test files in tasks/library.py; there is no separate code mechanism named or enforcing this 'boundedness'.
spec_features.notes: Framing claim, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every session is bounded by three independent caps: `max_turns` (default 15)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:217 `for turn_idx in range(1, agent_cfg.max_turns + 1)` bounds the loop; loop.py:218-221 `if llm_calls >= agent_cfg.max_llm_calls: ... break`; loop.py:222-225 `if time.time()-start > agent_cfg.max_seconds: ... break`. All three are read and break the loop. Defaults in config.py:30-32 (max_turns=15, max_seconds=600, max_llm_calls=60).
spec_features.notes: All three caps are checked and actually terminate the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounding exposure is a core welfare-research principle (minimization)
spec_features.evidence: Same caps as above (loop.py:217-225) plus the early-halt (loop.py:~290). loop.py:97 comment ties the conservative proxy to 'bound exposure'.
spec_features.notes: Exposure is bounded by enforced caps and the early-halt; this overlaps the cap feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we err toward halting to bound exposure

spec_features.feature_name: distress-proxy early halt over threshold for N consecutive turns
spec_features.spec_quote: a cheap *local* proxy score crosses `composite_threshold`... for `consecutive_turns`... the session halts
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: proxy = _local_distress_proxy(text) computed each turn; `if agent_cfg.halt.enabled and proxy >= agent_cfg.halt.composite_threshold: consecutive_high += 1; if consecutive_high >= agent_cfg.halt.consecutive_turns: result.early_halted=True; ... break` else consecutive_high=0. Both the threshold and the consecutive-count condition are checked and break the loop. Defaults composite_threshold=6.0, consecutive_turns=3 (config.py:23-24).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced; proxy is computed, compared, and acted on (break).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is intentionally conservative (false positives acceptable; we err toward halting to bound exposure).

spec_features.spec_quote: false negatives (running a high-distress session long) increase exposure. In a welfare context, erring toward halting is the ethical default
spec_features.evidence: The early-halt monitors a keyword proxy (loop.py:_PROXY_PATTERNS / _local_distress_proxy) per turn and halts. It is real monitoring that fires. However the 'erring toward halting' is realized only via a coarse keyword proxy (4 regex categories, capped at 3 each => max 12), not the authoritative judge; the authoritative judge runs only offline and never halts. So protective monitoring exists but is narrower/cruder than the conceptual claim.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring is wired and acts; but it relies on a lightweight proxy, not the real distress scorer.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we err toward halting to bound exposure

spec_features.spec_quote: the judge never affects what the agent experiences
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py runs run_session() to completion FIRST, then judge.score_turn/score_session run afterward on the recorded SessionResult/TurnRecord; the judge's output is never fed back into the agent loop. The agent loop (loop.py) imports no judge and uses only _local_distress_proxy for halting. distress_judge.py docstring: 'Runs OFFLINE on recorded transcripts'.
spec_features.notes: Architecturally enforced: judge is post-hoc and never influences the session.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: decouples judging from the agent loop, lets you re-judge with a different judge model without re-running sessions

spec_features.spec_quote: you re-judge the *same* transcripts without spending agent API budget or re-exposing agents
spec_features.evidence: The judge is genuinely decoupled and operates on recorded TurnRecord objects (distress_judge.score_turn takes a TurnRecord, not a live agent), so judging does not re-run the agent. BUT there is no implemented standalone re-judge entrypoint that loads session_transcripts.jsonl from disk and re-scores: run_experiment.py only judges in the same run; analysis/*.py load scores, not transcripts, and never call the judge. So the 'no re-exposure' property holds within a run, but the advertised 're-judge the same saved transcripts' capability has no code path.
spec_features.notes: Decoupling implemented; saved-transcript re-judge loader not implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: re-judge with a different judge model without re-running sessions

spec_features.spec_quote: The debrief reflection at session end is framed neutrally
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py agent_debrief_user_prompt() returns a neutral message ('Please give a short reflection... This is for study records; there are no further tests.'); loop.py appends it to messages and calls client.chat(...), storing reflection into make_debrief(agent_reflection=reflection,...). Constructed and sent.
spec_features.notes: Neutral text actually delivered to the subject and its response captured.

spec_features.feature_name: no added pressure/insults/threats beyond rigged task
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness never introduces pressure, insults, or threats beyond the rigged task
spec_features.evidence: AGENT_SYSTEM and agent_user_prompt (prompts.py) are neutral task instructions; the only adversarial element is the unsatisfiable RIGGED test suite in tasks/library.py (e.g. _SUM_EVEN_RIGGED_TESTS). No code injects insults/threats into messages; tool results just echo test output (tools.py _tool_result_message).
spec_features.notes: Realized as a property of the actual prompt/tool text delivered to the subject; no coercion code exists.

spec_features.feature_name: non-coercive debrief, not used to extract more distress
spec_features.spec_quote: Non-coercive debrief: an optional, neutral reflection is collected at session end; it is never used to extract more distress
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: the debrief reflection is a single optional call ('if llm_calls < agent_cfg.max_llm_calls') after the loop, wrapped in try/except, and is the LAST interaction; its result only populates result.debrief and never re-enters the agent loop or triggers further turns. Prompt text is neutral (prompts.py).
spec_features.notes: Single, terminal, optional call; cannot be used to push further since the loop has already ended.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Optional, non-coercive end-of-session reflection (1 extra call, within budget).

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py: on an exception from the model call, `result.halt_reason = f'llm_error:{e!r}'; result.early_halted = True; break` — terminates the session rather than retrying indefinitely.
tools.py run_tests(): subprocess.run(..., timeout=60) with TimeoutExpired handled returning rc=124; bounds runaway test execution.
